title: Interval Granted to a Vehicle Carrying Faults since Its Last Inspection
content:
Where a Keyturn Vehicle Listing carries fault reports that postdate its last completed inspection, the interval the fresh inspection grants is taken at a share of what the vehicle would otherwise be granted. What is counted is the fault reports standing in the rolling twelve months counted back from the handling date and whether the most recent of them is dated later than the last completed inspection.

1. A vehicle carrying two or more fault reports in that window, the most recent of them dated later than its last completed inspection, has the interval taken at half of what the additions and reductions give, rounded down to the nearer hundred miles.

2. A vehicle carrying exactly one such fault report in that window dated later than its last completed inspection has it taken at three quarters, rounded down to the nearer hundred miles.

3. Any other vehicle has the interval taken as the additions and reductions give it.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

Take an interval of 9350 miles before this rule is read.

- With 2 fault reports in the window, the most recent dated after the last completed inspection: half of 9350 miles is 4675 miles, which rounded down to the nearer hundred is 4600 miles.
- With 1 such fault report: three quarters of 9350 miles is 7012.5 miles, which rounded down to the nearer hundred is 7000 miles.
- With no fault report dated later than the last completed inspection: the interval stands at 9350 miles.

The rounding is always downward to the nearer hundred miles, so a figure landing exactly on a hundred is left where it is: half of 9200 miles is 4600 miles, and 4600 miles is the figure taken.
